stories.title: Google will cut off search access for students at schools that reject AI
stories.simple_summary: Google is saying it will stop letting students use Google Search if their schools don't accept AI tools. Schools would have to allow AI use to keep search access for their students.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have school-age grandchildren, this could affect whether they can use Google at school. For small business owners, this shows how aggressively companies are pushing AI into places where people might not want it.

stories.title: Google researchers are fighting the company to tell the world what they know about AI
stories.simple_summary: Google researchers want to tell the public things they've learned about AI risks. The company may be stopping them from speaking publicly.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people interested in AI safety. It doesn't directly change anything you need to do, but it's worth knowing that employees sometimes want to share information their bosses prefer to keep quiet.

stories.title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
stories.simple_summary: A big website where people share custom additions for games now requires creators to say whether they used AI to help make their mods. This is about being honest and transparent.
stories.why_it_matters: If you play PC games or have hobbies online, you'll now know which additions used AI. For small business owners, this shows how accountability for AI is becoming normal.

stories.title: Please stop asking me when the AI bubble will pop
stories.simple_summary: A writer is tired of people asking when AI investment will crash and lose money. Nobody actually knows the answer, including experts.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors. If you're not investing in AI companies, there's nothing here you need to worry about.

stories.title: CrowdStrike's new kill switch can stop rogue AI agents in their tracks, CEO says
stories.simple_summary: CrowdStrike, a security company, says it has created a way to stop AI agents that misbehave or go out of control. It's like an emergency brake for rogue AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly for tech companies and investors. For ordinary people and small business owners, this doesn't require any action on your part.

stories.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
stories.simple_summary: A company called Anthropic is building a system to verify that an AI response actually came from the AI it claims to be from. It's like checking a signature on a letter to make sure it's real.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech specialists and investors. As AI becomes more common, having ways to verify it's real AI will matter more, but right now there's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Data centers are turning to old jet engines as the wait for power grows
stories.simple_summary: Companies building data centers for AI are using old jet engines to power them because there aren't enough new power sources available. Jet engines work but waste energy and harm the environment.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that AI is using so much power that power grids can't keep up. Long-term, everyone's electricity bills could be affected as energy becomes harder to access.

stories.title: Google says there’s no way to use Search without using artificial intelligence
stories.simple_summary: Google says that Search now always uses artificial intelligence in the background. You can't use Search without it anymore, whether you know it's happening or not.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google Search, AI is already helping find your results. You don't have to do anything, but it's good to know Google's core product now depends on AI.

stories.title: Ted Schlein’s Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for new funds amid AI-driven cybersecurity boom
stories.simple_summary: An investment company that focuses on cybersecurity is trying to raise a large amount of money. They believe AI is making cybersecurity more important and valuable.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors. For small business owners, it signals that spending on security to protect against hackers will probably keep increasing.

stories.title: As artificial intelligence advances and the labor market improves, the country will not need to accept so many foreign workers under the Specified Skilled Worker program.
stories.simple_summary: Japan's government is saying it may not need to bring in as many foreign workers because AI and a stronger job market could fill some of those positions.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly important if you follow international labor policy. For most people, it doesn't directly affect daily life.

stories.title: AMD forecast eases AI spending fears as data-center sales surge
stories.simple_summary: The computer chip company AMD sold more products than expected, especially for data centers that run AI. This suggests companies are still spending heavily on AI infrastructure.
stories.why_it_matters: For small business owners, this shows that large companies are continuing to invest in AI, which means AI tools will probably keep improving and becoming more available.

stories.title: Hiding inside Palantir’s skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal
stories.simple_summary: The company Palantir, which does data analysis work, just made more money from regular businesses than from the government for the first time. This shows the company is growing in the regular business world.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching the company's growth. For small business owners, it suggests that data analysis tools from big tech companies are becoming more widespread in regular companies.
